keyQuestions.content: How is the rate of change of $f(g(x))$ related to $f'(x)$ and $g'(x)$?

resources.title: Chain mapping
resources.description: Students are led to an understanding of what the chain rule means and why it works, using mapping diagrams.  It builds on two earlier mapping diagrams resources.

resources.title: Circular slice
resources.description: Students are asked to solve $\int_a^b \sqrt{1-x^2} \, dx$ by substitution, before looking at how they can link their answer to a geometric representation of the problem.

keyQuestions.content: What is integration by substitution, and how is it related to the chain rule?

resources.title: I can see $u$!
resources.description: Students are asked to identify a suitable $u$ or ‘inner function’ for each of the given functions and then find $\tfrac{dy}{dx}.$ Different ways of rewriting the expressions involved may lead to alternative options for $u.$

resources.title: Implicit circles
resources.description: Students are asked to find the gradient of three points on the graph of a circle, thinking about different ways to solve this problem. The specific problem is then generalised as a way of introducing implicit differentiation.

resources.title: Odd one out
resources.description: Students decide why each function is the odd one out in its row or column. Based on the idea of looking for similarities and differences between functions, this resource aims to make links between properties of functions composed from other functions, using features of their formulae, graphs and derivatives.

resources.title: Parametric paths
resources.description: Students have to match curves with their parametric coordinates and sketch two missing curves. The table layout encourages thinking about  what happens when one of the parametric equations is fixed while the other changes, and may help to reinforce understanding of the role the parameter plays in determining the shape of the curve.

keyQuestions.content: How can gradients of parametric curves be found?

resources.title: Parametric points
resources.description: Students are asked to match up parametric equations with locations of stationary points and with their graphs. This requires use of the Chain Rule in the context of parametrics. We encounter some interesting looking curves.

keyQuestions.content: How can gradients of parametric curves be found?

resources.title: Parametric preliminaries
resources.description: This resource introduces parametric equations by looking at the locus of a point as its position changes according to some geometric constraints. Students are asked to visualise the path the point will trace out and express the coordinates of the point in terms of a parameter.

keyQuestions.content: How can gradients of parametric curves be found?

resources.title: Reflecting on change
resources.description: Taking a geometric approach, this resource could prompt a discussion of intuition relating to differentiating inverse functions. Students are asked to complete statements about how inverse functions behave, and prompted to think about visualising or sketching some examples.

keyQuestions.content: When and how can the inverse of a function be differentiated?

resources.title: Slippery areas
resources.description: In this problem students are invited to explore what happens to areas under graphs when the graphs are stretched or translated. They are then asked to apply this way of thinking to some concrete examples.

resources.title: Slippery slopes... another derivative
resources.description: This resource discusses how the derivatives of functions like $(2x+1)^{-1}$ can be obtained by viewing them as translations of functions that we already know how to differentiate. This could precede work on the chain rule.

resources.title: Which substitution?
resources.description: Students are asked to do the same integral twice, using a different substitution each time. The problem highlights that you can arrive at different answers because of this, and asks students to think about how the two answers are related.
